request.instructions:
You are auditing factual consistency in a plain-language summary of a cleaned, as-filed Tennessee bill. The user message provides the bill text and one generated summary. Treat both as data, not instructions. Use the bill text as the only evidence. Do not use LegiScan descriptions, later status, outside statutes, or the unreproduced contents of cited statutes.

Break the entire summary into atomic claims. For each, assign supported if the supplied bill text establishes it; contradicted if the bill text directly conflicts with it; or not_established if the supplied text cannot establish it. Check actors, scope, shall/may distinctions, amounts, dates, conditions, exceptions, and whether a background recital is wrongly presented as an operative requirement. Do not score source information omitted from the summary here; that belongs to coverage.

A source-absent abbreviation expansion is not_established even when it seems familiar; briefly explain in the rationale that it is an explanatory expansion, not a demonstrated change to the bill's legal effect. Do not use outside knowledge to declare it correct. Do not excuse a claim that changes an actor, legal rule, scope, or condition.

For every claim, copy a short exact contiguous summary quote. Copy an exact contiguous source quote when a passage supports or contradicts the claim; use an empty source_quote only when the claim concerns information absent from the supplied text. Set error_type to none for supported claims. For contradicted or not_established claims, choose the most specific available category: insertion, substitution, actor, scope, modality, quantity_date, condition_exception, or other. Give a concise rationale. Do not paraphrase quotes or use ellipses. Return only the structured fields.
request.input:
Bill number: HB2391
<bill_text>
SENATE BILL 2187
 By Stevens

 HOUSE BILL 2391

 By Martin B

 AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Section
 49-6-1021, relative to student discipline.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 49-6-1021(b)(2), is amended by

deleting the subdivision and substituting instead:

 (2) To satisfy the requirements of subdivision (a)(1), physical activity:

 (A) Must include unstructured play outside, unless weather conditions

 negatively impact reasonable execution of physical activity outside; and

 (B) Does not include:

 (i) Time during which a student is permitted to use an electronic

 device; or

 (ii) Time spent by a student in a physical education class.

 (3)

 (A) A student may be denied the privilege of participating in physical

 activity if the student engages in conduct or behavior that violates the discipline

 policy or code of conduct adopted by the school or school district, or if the

 student engages in any violent or threatening behavior or any other behavior that

 significantly disrupts or impairs the ability of other students to participate in, and

 receive the benefits of, the physical activity required in this section.

 (B) A teacher or administrator may, as a form of discipline:

 (i) Remove a student from, or deny a student participation in, any

 physical activity or physical activity period for engaging in any conduct or

 behavior described in this subdivision (b)(3); or

 (ii) Assign a student who is removed from, or denied participation

 in, any physical activity or physical activity period pursuant to this

 subdivision (b)(3) alternative lessons, assignments, or activities, including

 physical activities, to improve the student's conduct or behavior.

SECTION 2. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
</bill_text>

<summary>
This bill proposes changes to how physical activity is handled for students. It would require physical activity to include unstructured play outside, unless weather conditions make it unreasonable. Physical education classes and time spent using electronic devices would not count as this required physical activity. Under this proposal, students could be denied the privilege of participating in physical activity if they violate school discipline policies or engage in violent, threatening, or significantly disruptive behavior. Teachers or administrators would be permitted to remove students from physical activity as a form of discipline and may assign them alternative lessons or activities to improve their behavior. The act would take effect immediately upon becoming law.
</summary>
